A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same PLLB research. Their main text, equations, figures, tables, and appendices are readable and support comparison, including matching SelectSay in v1 to SaySelect in v2.

before.justification: V1 reports original agent experiments on four tasks and human studies involving maze solving and image reconstruction, with results in Figures 4–10 and appendix rule examples.

after.justification: V2 retains these original results and adds robot grasp experiments, an LM-only maze control, and comparisons of rules generated by different models.

M1.justification: The core rule-generation and policy-update loop remains unchanged. V2 adds a localized GRASP implementation combining a language-regularized neural contextual-bandit keypoint selector with a fixed Sphinx trajectory planner (Section 8, Appendix A.1). Newly disclosed details for retained tasks do not establish changes to their methods.

E1.justification: V2 adds physical robot grasp planning, substantially extending coverage beyond the original four tasks. GRASP includes transfer to a different bag, location, and visual distractors (Sections 8.1–8.3). SelectSay/SaySelect is a renamed retained task.

E2.justification: Section 6.1 adds an evaluated LM-only maze policy without Q-value updates. GRASP introduces comparisons with Vanilla RL and a zero-shot Molmo-guided Oracle, alongside the adversarial-rule variant. ReAct, Reflexion, and Rememberer are discussed rather than directly evaluated as named baselines.

E3.justification: GRASP introduces a substantial new protocol: a planner trained on 50 trajectories, a 100-by-100 keypoint action space, and success, missed-grasp, and torque-based rewards. V2 also adds the maze control and model configurations in Appendix B.2. Appendix A.1's newly disclosed settings for existing experiments do not establish protocol revisions.

E4.justification: V2 adds a control testing whether maze solving works without Q-value updates, robot robustness tests under changed objects and surroundings, and Appendix B.2's qualitative analysis of model size and rule quality. These extend the questions tested beyond the retained adversarial-rule and maze-transfer analyses.

E5.justification: Section 8.2 explicitly reports averaging GRASP results over 20 random seeds, adding seed-count reporting absent from v1. This concerns the new experiment, not an established increase in runs. Existing human-study significance tests and corrections are retained.

E6.justification: V2 adds GRASP learning and transfer curves (Figure 11), 0% success for the LM-only maze control using final PLLB rules (Section 6.1), and model-dependent qualitative findings (Appendix B.2). Figure 11 supports faster learning; several standard-setting comparators eventually reach the same reward. The original principal comparisons and Tables 1–4 are retained.

T1.justification: The MDP formalization, language-regularized Q-learning equations, and BIRDS reward definition remain unchanged. Neither version supplies theoretical propositions or proofs, and v2 adds no substantive formal derivation.

C1.justification: V2 retains the central interpretability, generalization, and human-coordination claims while extending explicit performance and generalization contributions to robot grasp planning. Applicability when language cannot express the entire policy was already claimed in v1, although v2 foregrounds it.

C2.justification: V2 adds interpretations concerning nonlinguistic policy learning, visual-feature overreliance, and model-dependent rule failures. It qualifies the earlier robotics caveat using GRASP while retaining the long-horizon sensorimotor limitation. Appendix B.2 also offers tentative explanations involving model training and keypoint recognition.

D1.justification: New Appendix A.1 substantially improves implementation disclosure across tasks: regularization strengths, rule ensembles and selection, BART training budgets, Stable Diffusion settings, and GRASP learning parameters. Section 8 and Appendix A.5 add robot architecture, training, and prompt details. The source-code access information is retained.

R1.justification: V2 sharpens comparisons with text-based agents, adds Rememberer and Kim et al. (2020), and introduces robotics and physical-grounding references, including Gao et al., Kalashnikov et al., and Sundaresan et al. The overarching positioning around language's cognitive and communicative functions remains intact.

P1.justification: V2 selectively rewrites the abstract, introduction, related-work discussion, method explanations, and limitations; renames SelectSay to SaySelect; and inserts robotics and appendix subsections. Much of the original exposition and its overall sequence are retained.

P2.justification: V2 adds a GRASP column to Figure 2, robot Figures 11 and 15, and Table 5. It improves Figure 5's axis labels and training-budget annotation, adjusts other displays, and reformats retained rule tables. These are localized additions and refinements within the existing visual structure.

improvement.justification: V2 substantially strengthens the central argument through the maze control and physical robot learning and transfer evidence, while Appendix A.1 resolves important implementation omissions in v1. These gains improve both evidential support and reproducibility. The model comparison remains primarily qualitative, and the claim of higher final GRASP reward is stronger than Figure 11 supports, but these limitations do not outweigh the overall gains.
